modes.label: Anka Build AMI on AWS EC2 Mac (Marketplace hourly software fee)
modes.note: Software fee ONLY, per hour of EC2 Mac instance uptime, independent of how many macOS VMs run on the host. The AWS EC2 Mac dedicated-host charge (24-hour minimum allocation) is billed separately by AWS and is NOT included. 365-day contracts: Basic ARM $2,200 (mac2/mac2-m2) to $5,000 (m1ultra); Enterprise ARM $2,640-$6,500; Enterprise Plus ARM $2,880-$7,500; Intel mac1.metal Basic $3,600 / Enterprise $4,680 / Enterprise Plus $5,880 per year. Marketplace-only procurement, via AWS account.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.
caveats: No public price (contact sales); licence only — the Mac hardware is yours (own, EC2 Mac, MacStadium ...).
Apple SLA: max 2 extra macOS VMs per Mac.
Anka Develop is free (one VM on a laptop, not for CI).

AWS Marketplace listings (seller Veertu Inc, linked from veertu.com/aws-marketplace and docs 'Use our AWS Marketplace AMI with hourly billing for Anka') give the only public Anka prices: software $0.28-$1.15 per EC2 Mac host-hour depending on tier and Mac model; AWS host cost (24 h minimum) is extra. A BYOL Community AMI also exists.

Anka Flow licence (developer Macs/iMacs, run multiple VMs, push/pull registry) is priced per machine; Anka Crypt (disposable macOS VMs for coding agents) and Anka MCP are free MIT open-source add-ons that need an Anka install.
Suspend/state snapshot of a VM is Intel-only; on Apple Silicon there is no memory suspend (pause_resume false stands).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.note: Stopping a VM shuts it down and the VM disk persists locally (persistent disk, not a snapshot). Controller instances are ephemeral clones of a template tag. Nothing is saved automatically: saving state to the registry is always an explicit 'Save Template Image' request or 'anka push'.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Description: Create a “Save Image” request. Save a running VM instance to the Registry as a new Tag or Template.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Available via the Controller REST API (POST /api/v1/image) or the CLI ('anka push' / local tag). The saved tag is a template: new VMs clone or start from it on any node ('Once a VM has been tagged, it becomes a “VM Template”'). Memory is included only on Intel: the 'suspend' option (default true) suspends before pushing, but 'ARM USERS: From the CLI: suspending will currently stop the VM', so on Apple Silicon the snapshot is disk only.

harness_api.quote: Crypt is a helper binary that automates this workflow. It clones a prepared base Anka VM, runs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, and others) inside the clone, and handles mount, SSH, and cleanup for you. Run crypt claude or crypt codex from a project directory for an interactive session, or crypt claude --mount "your prompt" / crypt codex --mount "your prompt" for an unattended task run.
harness_api.note: Crypt is Veertu's first-party, MIT-licensed, local host-side CLI. It launches Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Cursor Agent CLI or Sakana Fugu in YOLO mode with a prompt and keeps the clone between sessions ('crypt claude --mount . "keep going"'). It works by wrapping SSH/anka run: output goes to the terminal, with no event API or conversation list/resume API. There is no REST harness API in the Controller. The Anka MCP server manages VMs, not harnesses.

egress_allowlist.quote: Filter rules can block local traffic, block inbound services, allow only approved destinations, or deny specific sensitive endpoints.
egress_allowlist.note: Host-side, per-VM/template IP filtering in ipf.conf style (Anka 3.3+), e.g. 'pass out to 10.20.30.40' followed by 'block any'. It works on IPs, ports and 'local'; there are no hostnames. Other options: network modes 'host' ('can’t access external networks outside of the host') and 'disconnected', and --no-local. The filter is enforced by the hypervisor on the host, so a root user in the guest cannot undo it. 'Advanced network security features require an Enterprise or Enterprise Plus license.'

ingress_rules.note: Inbound traffic is controlled per VM by filter rules (e.g. 'block in to port 22', 'pass in from 10.20.30.40'). Only the ports you add are exposed on the host: 'anka modify add port', or the Controller's port_forwarding_override ('Any pre-existing rules will be ignored and ONLY the ones specified made available'). --no-local blocks VM-host traffic. Bridge mode and VLAN tags are also available. Nothing is exposed to the public internet by Anka; that depends on your host network.

guest_firewall.note: Each guest is a full macOS VM (Apple Virtualization / Anka hypervisor) with an admin user who has sudo, so pf inside the guest works. Its rules are separate from Anka's host-side filter.

secret_proxy.quote: Scope credentials to the project and operation. Do not give the VM broad GitHub, cloud, password manager, or internal network tokens unless the task requires them.
secret_proxy.note: There is no first-party credential-injecting proxy. Agent credentials live inside the VM: the base VM is logged in or given API keys in ~/.zprofile (Crypt README), and the Controller startup_script accepts ENVs such as TOKEN=123.

volume_attach.note: 'anka modify <vm> add disk' attaches an extra disk image or host device (sata/virtio-blk, --ro or --rw). Host directories can also be shared into a running VM with 'anka mount' (VirtioFS, Apple Silicon, Anka 3.9+). Both are local to the Mac host; there are no network/block volumes, since Anka is self-hosted on your Macs.
